main_text.p: huic societati se addiderunt. Nec obscura est causa, cur incrementa tam felicia societas haec ceperit, & ex rebus, melioribus ad vires regibus formidabiles brevi pervenerit. Quippe olim etiam & multo ante auctam Macedonum potentiam cum statu populari regerentur, tanta justitiae & aequitatis laude florue-re Achaei, ut in Italia quoque quae nominis Graeci civitates erant, cum domi res vehementer turbatas haberent, & crudelibus odiis intestinis post caedes civiles laborarent, ex omni populorum Graecorum numero horum solorum autoritatem & consilia secutae concordiam instaurarint, imo & post aliquot[?] annos ad eorum exemplar respubli[?] compofuerint. Adde, quod eodem cit[?], quòd post pugnam Leuctricam Graecorum omnium animis vehementer attonitis, cum eorum, qui dimicaverant, pars utraque victoriam sibi adscriberet, utrique arbitrio solorum Achaeorum litem illam submiserint, non quòd ii opibus praevalerent, (erant enim eae tunc, ut ait Polybius, in tota fere Graecia minimae) sed quòd fides eorum & probitas supra caeteros omnes praedicarentur. page.notes: Doubtful readings: "aliquot" and "respubli" are overlaid by show-through from the reverse, so the final letters are uncertain. "eodem cit" is partly obscured by show-through; the word between "eodem" and "cit" is not legible. Show-through text (such as the fragments near "aliquot" and "eodem") was not transcribed. The leading "se" in the first line appears as "fe" in the scan and is read as "se" with some doubt; the line is marked as a continuation from the previous page. The line ends with the hyphenated "fa-", which continues on the next page.
